text.p: Spanish government bonds took a roller-coaster ride on Thursday; bonos were recovering from previous losses on better-than-expected U.S. data when the news that Yelstin fired security chief Alexander Lebed hit markets.
"We fell in line with the Bund," a dealer explained.

But shortly afterwards the market had recovered a little and was heading up again, with futures stabbing at resistance at 106.29. After Wednesday's heavy losses, Spanish bonds were deriving some support from short-covering, dealers said.
But recent declarations by Bundesbank officials clouded Spain's outlook to qualify for the single currency from 1999.
"In the short term we will see people buying on the dip, but in a couple of weeks' time it is likely bonos will consolidate more," an analyst said.
The 10-year spread over German bunds was at 184 basis points, little changed from 182 at Wednesday's close but well off the 155 basis points low it touched a week ago.

On the cash market, the 10-year benchmark was recovering at 105.98 from 105.84 at the previous close, while the three-year 7.80 percent bond was almost unchanged at 102.60 from 102.61 at Wednesday's close.
